messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran into a weird authoring/validation mismatch in Console preflight. Saved a route with quotas and YAML anchors, Console linter showed green, runtime rejected it at serving time. Anyone seen anchor/merge expansion differences between our schema validator and runtime?

jake: hmm. Can you paste the YAML you used?

maria: pasted a minimal repro:

maria: ```yaml
defaults: &q
  requests_per_minute: 1000
  burst: 200

routes:
  - match: /api/v1/*
    quota: *q
    labels:
      team: payments
```

nora: That looks fine on the surface. What error did the runtime give?

maria: runtime error: `invalid field "quota": expected object with explicit fields [rate_limit window]` (we've got older runtime parsing looking for `rate_limit` structure not `requests_per_minute`)

jake: oh — schema and console accept the shorthand `requests_per_minute` because our JSON schema has a `oneOf` that includes both shapes, but the runtime unmarshaler only supports the `rate_limit` variant.

ethan: cc @sophie this is the sort of mismatch lint was supposed to catch during preflight. Sophie, were you working on the schema consolidations?

sophie: yea, I merged the two quota representations earlier to be lenient for authors. But I forgot the runtime compatibility gate. Console uses the JSON schema validator which accepts both. Runtime uses the old strict Go struct. My bad — we need a canonicalizer in the preflight that expands/shapes to runtime format.

maria: to be clear — the Console allowed the saved route and even showed a preview, but the serving cluster rejected at apply. That caused a brief 500s spike for a canary. Deploy-bot posted the failure in incidents.

jake: can we make lint rule that rejects the shorthand unless we canonicalize it? Or auto-transform the document on save to `rate_limit` shape?

nora: auto-transform feels nice for DX but dangerous for auditing (we want diffable YAML). Alternative: keep author-friendly shorthand but add an autofix suggestion (non-destructive) and a blocking preflight check that simulates runtime parsing.

ethan: I prefer a simulation check. It ensures what Console shows equals runtime behavior. We could run a dry-parse step using the same Go unmarshaler we ship. If parse fails, preflight fails with a clear message and suggestion.

sophie: agree. I'll add a `runtime-parse` validator to preflight. Also we should add a unit test matrix for anchors/merge keys because we just hit subtle anchor resolution differences between JS YAML parser and Go's `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` behavior.

maria: cc @ci-bot — we added a test in the branch and CI failed on a yaml-merge case.

ci-bot: build #5423 failed: tests/routes/authoring/anchor_repro_test.go:42 assertion failed — expected successful ParseToRuntime(), got parse error: line 3: merge key collision. Full log: https://ci.internal/redwood/5423/console

jake: ok — we need two things: (1) a test harness that runs the exact runtime parser in preflight so Console and runtime share behavior; (2) a clear UX in the console when autofix is available vs when the author must fix the source file.

nora: proposal: add a small inline hint panel in the editor that says "Preflight runtime-parse failed — click to preview autofix". Clicking shows an expanded view with the canonicalized YAML (rate_limit shape) and a one-click apply or copy.

sophie: that UX works. I'll prototype. For the immediate patch: making preflight blocking on runtime-parse should prevent future canary incidents. Will push a hotfix branch.

maria: thanks. Also a reminder: anchors can hide oddities (zero-width spaces etc.) — we should add a sanitizer pass that normalizes whitespace before runtime parse. That would have caught the invisible char in my original file.

ethan: +1 to sanitizer. Also add a lint that warns when using anchors for quota objects (we can recommend named `quota:` blocks instead of anchors).

jake: will create tickets: ENG-PLATFORM-902 (runtime-parse preflight), ENG-PLATFORM-903 (sanitizer + whitespace normalization), ENG-PLATFORM-904 (editor autofix preview).

sophie: pushing fix branch now. I'll link the PR after CI passes.

maria: excellent. thanks all :thumbsup:

ci-bot: PR #814 linked: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-platform/pull/814 — tests currently flaky, re-run queued.
